cuaTitle.text: Chat & Cua Spaces (Oct 21): delegate to Codex in a Linux desktop, then take the screen yourself

cuaFlow.text:
The flow

Message → pick or create a Space → chat → the desktop strip above the composer → Watch → Take control → full screen → Done → back to watching.

A Space is a Linux desktop. Codex works inside it. The chat is the main surface; the desktop is evidence, not a second app.

TAKING CONTROL PAUSES THE AGENT, NOT THE SPACE. The desktop, its apps and its downloads keep running the whole time.

Sending another chat message hands control back to Codex. That is the only way it resumes, and the handoff board says so on screen.

Done exits control, returns to watching and puts the phone back in portrait.

cuaReused.text:
Reused, not reinvented

• List rows, status dots and the three-line row: s2-list. No buttons in rows.
• Host dots, the glass Search/••• capsule and the floating dock: s2-list. Message is a third tab.
• Offline host = the hollow amber ring from dA2-sessions, row at 50%.
• Top bar, centred title and status line, glass back and tools: s2-view.
• User bubble #355C8F on #F2F2F7: bub-soft, the picked option.
• Composer, model chip, Stop that becomes Send on typing: s2-view.
• Queued and not-sent as a soft strip above the composer, with the row menu: s2-queued and s2-queued-failed.
• Tool steps grouped and expanded inline over a 1.5pt rule: s2-view.
• Bottom panel with eyebrow, title, card and no Dismiss: s2-signin-prompt.
• Sheet scaffold, drag indicator, 34pt corners: NewSessionSheets.
• Mac titlebar, tab strip, host strip and time-column rows: dA2-sessions.
• iPad 320pt sidebar card and the #182B3E selected row: ip-session.

New only where nothing existed: the desktop stage, and the manual-control chrome.

cuaDecisions.text:
Decisions worth arguing with

1. THE STAGE, NOT A TAB. A Chat/Desktop tab pair would hide one to show the other. The desktop instead lives in the slot S2 gives its pill row: a 44pt live strip at rest, a 229pt player when you tap Watch. The chat never leaves the screen and the transcript only gives up 185pt.

2. CONTROLLING IS A MODE, NOT A STATUS. It gets no sixth dot colour. It gets a 3pt accent ring around the whole screen and a blue “You have control” chip, next to an amber “Agent paused” chip. Watching has neither, so the two read apart in a thumbnail.

3. SPACE POWER LIVES IN THE SPACE SHEET. “Stop this Space” is one sheet away, under its own Space heading, never beside the composer’s Stop. Stop-the-turn stops the agent; Stop-the-Space closes the desktop. Two words that far apart cannot be fat-fingered.

4. NOTHING IS SENT UNTIL IT IS CONFIRMED. The agent writes a draft in Gmail and says so. The ask panel shows the real recipient, subject and body, and the footnote reads “Nothing has been sent.” The second button is Keep it as a draft, not Cancel.

5. NO JARGON FOR PERMISSION. “Let this Space read a folder?” with the folder name, the host and “read-only”. No mounts, no bind paths, no container words anywhere.

6. DARK ONLY, like every S2 and iPad board on this canvas. A light pass belongs with the Sessions light pass, not alone here.

cuaGestures.text:
Manual control: the gesture map

• One finger, tap or drag — the guest cursor. Tap, drag, select.
• Two-finger tap — right-click.
• Two fingers, drag — pan the local viewport. Never reaches the desktop.
• Pinch — zoom, 1× to 4×. The factor shows beside Fit once past 1×.
• Fit — back to the whole desktop, centred, at 1×.

One finger is the guest and two fingers are the local view: that split is the whole model, and the hint strip states it in four pairs rather than an onboarding sheet.

Chrome stays to Done, Fit and Keyboard. Portrait fits the desktop to width (390×244) and says to turn the phone; landscape fits to height (624×390). Landscape-right is landscape-left mirrored — the chrome insets on whichever side the sensor housing is.

The keyboard row carries what a Linux desktop needs and iOS will not send: esc, tab, ctrl, alt, arrows, return.
